title: True or False: The Definition of Done ensures that each Increment meets the agreed quality standards before it is considered complete. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done establishes the shared quality standards for each Increment, ensuring that all completed work meets the agreed criteria. The Definition of Done helps Scrum Teams improve quality by clarifying what’s needed for each Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done sets the minimum quality criteria that each Increment must meet to be considered complete.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is specifically designed to define the criteria for completed work and ensure quality standards are met.

title: True or False: The Definition of Done should be adjusted frequently during Sprints to accommodate changing quality standards. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done should be adjusted during Retrospectives, not during ongoing Sprints, to ensure stable quality standards. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done should be stable during Sprints and revised thoughtfully outside of active work periods.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done should be reviewed and adjusted during Sprint Retrospectives, not within ongoing Sprints.

title: Which three practices can help the Scrum Team to enhance the quality of the Increment? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Enhancing the Increment’s quality involves updating the Definition of Done, using feedback sessions, and implementing automated testing. The Definition of Done helps Scrum Teams improve quality by clarifying what’s needed for each Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Regularly updating the Definition of Done as the team learns and improves.
explanation1: Correct: An evolving Definition of Done reflects continuous improvement in quality standards.
answer2: Having the Scrum Master inspect the Increment regularly.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Developers are responsible for quality; the Scrum Master facilitates, not inspects.
answer3: Conducting frequent collaborative reviews and feedback sessions.
explanation3: Correct: Regular reviews help identify issues early and improve quality.
answer4: Using automated testing to verify work meets the Definition of Done.
explanation4: Correct: Automated testing ensures that the Increment meets quality standards efficiently.
answer5: Documenting every change in detail before implementation.
explanation5: Incorrect: Excessive documentation can slow down progress without adding significant value.

title: Which three elements should be included in the Definition of Done? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Definition of Done sets quality standards, includes compliance criteria, and establishes testing requirements to ensure completed work meets agreed standards. The Definition of Done helps Scrum Teams improve quality by clarifying what’s needed for each Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: A checklist of daily tasks for each Developer.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is not a task list; it sets quality standards.
answer2: Quality standards that must be met for work to be considered complete.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done includes all quality criteria that define completeness.
answer3: Compliance with relevant regulations and organizational standards.
explanation3: Correct: The Definition of Done often includes adherence to regulations and standards.
answer4: The Product Owner’s sign-off on completed work.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done focuses on quality, not individual approvals.
answer5: Agreed criteria for testing and validating completed work.
explanation5: Correct: Testing and validation ensure the work meets quality and completeness standards.

title: Which two actions can help a Scrum Team maintain a consistent focus on quality throughout the Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Regularly reviewing the Definition of Done and integrating quality checks into Daily Scrums help ensure consistent focus on quality throughout the Sprint. The Definition of Done helps ensure that quality standards are met consistently. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assigning a specific team member to be responsible for quality control.
explanation1: Incorrect: Quality is a collective responsibility, not an individual role within the Scrum Team.
answer2: Regularly reviewing the Definition of Done during refinement sessions to ensure it reflects current standards.
explanation2: Correct: Regular reviews of the Definition of Done help maintain and improve quality standards.
answer3: Including quality checks as part of the Daily Scrum discussions to identify and address potential issues early.
explanation3: Correct: Discussing quality during Daily Scrums helps the team stay aware of standards and address issues promptly.
answer4: Deferring all quality checks to the end of the Sprint to save time.
explanation4: Incorrect: Deferring quality checks increases the risk of defects and rework, impacting the Sprint Goal.
answer5: Reducing the Definition of Done criteria to make completion easier.
explanation5: Incorrect: Lowering standards compromises product quality and stakeholder trust.

title: A Scrum Team is struggling with low velocity and wants to improve. What actions should they consider? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Improving velocity involves refining the Product Backlog, continuously inspecting and adapting processes, and enhancing team collaboration. The Scrum Team’s inspect-and-adapt practices help them continuously improve. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Add more Developers to increase capacity.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding team members may temporarily disrupt the team dynamics and won’t immediately improve velocity.
answer2: Inspect and adapt their process during the Sprint Retrospective.
explanation2: Correct: Retrospectives are key opportunities to identify and implement improvements.
answer3: Ensure that all Product Backlog items are well-refined and ready for Sprint Planning.
explanation3: Correct: A well-refined backlog helps the team understand and commit to work that they can complete.
answer4: Increase working hours to fit more work into the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sustainable pace is crucial; overworking can lead to burnout.
answer5: Improve collaboration and communication within the team.
explanation5: Correct: Better collaboration can lead to more effective work and improved velocity.

title: Which two actions can help a Scrum Team improve their handling of technical debt? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Incorporating technical debt into the Definition of Done and conducting regular code reviews help Scrum Teams manage technical debt effectively, maintaining product quality. Technical debt management ensures sustainable product quality. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Including technical debt tasks only when all other Sprint work is completed.
explanation1: Incorrect: Technical debt should be managed continuously, not deferred until the end of Sprints.
answer2: Incorporating technical debt resolution into the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: Integrating technical debt into the Definition of Done ensures it is consistently addressed as part of the team's regular work.
answer3: Conducting regular code reviews to identify and resolve areas contributing to technical debt.
explanation3: Correct: Regular code reviews help catch issues early and manage technical debt proactively.
answer4: Ignoring technical debt in favor of focusing solely on new feature development.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring technical debt leads to a decrease in product quality and maintainability over time.
answer5: Assigning technical debt tasks to a specific team member responsible for clean-up.
explanation5: Incorrect: Technical debt management should be a shared responsibility within the team.

title: A Scrum Team consistently delivers increments that fail to meet stakeholder expectations. What should the Scrum Master do to address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a review of the Definition of Done and acceptance criteria to ensure that the team’s work aligns with stakeholder expectations and delivers value. The Scrum Team is responsible for all product development work, including ensuring quality meets stakeholder needs. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the team to work faster and harder to meet expectations.
explanation1: Incorrect: Working faster without addressing root causes can lead to poor quality and further dissatisfaction.
answer2: Facilitate a collaborative review of the Definition of Done and acceptance criteria to ensure alignment with stakeholder needs.
explanation2: Correct: Reviewing quality standards helps the team align their work with stakeholder expectations and deliver valuable increments.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to lower stakeholder expectations to match the team’s output.
explanation3: Incorrect: Reducing expectations does not address the need for improvement and alignment.
answer4: Ignore the feedback and focus on meeting internal team goals.
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback is crucial for driving improvement and ensuring the product delivers value.

title: A Scrum Team frequently misses their Definition of Done due to last-minute testing issues. How should the Scrum Master address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a discussion on integrating testing earlier in the process, helping the team consistently meet the Definition of Done. The Definition of Done helps ensure that quality standards are met. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Extend the Sprint to allow more time for testing and fixing issues.
explanation1: Incorrect: Extending Sprints disrupts the Scrum cadence and is not allowed.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on integrating testing earlier in the development process to catch issues sooner.
explanation2: Correct: Early integration of testing helps the team meet the Definition of Done consistently.
answer3: Assign a dedicated tester to the team to handle all testing tasks.
explanation3: Incorrect: Scrum promotes cross-functional teams; assigning dedicated roles is not a preferred approach.
answer4: Ignore the issue as testing challenges are part of software development.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring recurring issues prevents continuous improvement and may affect product quality.

title: A Scrum Team is struggling with integrating testing into their development process, leading to delays. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions on integrating testing early in the development process to help the team meet quality standards consistently. Testing is an integral part of the Definition of Done. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign a dedicated tester to handle all testing tasks for the team.
explanation1: Incorrect: Assigning a dedicated role undermines the cross-functional nature of the team.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on how to integrate testing earlier in the development process, such as through Test-Driven Development (TDD) or pairing.
explanation2: Correct: Early integration of testing helps the team deliver increments that meet quality standards consistently.
answer3: Ignore the issue and allow the team to manage testing as they see fit.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should support the team in improving their processes to avoid recurring delays.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to reduce the quality expectations to speed up testing.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reducing quality compromises the integrity of the product and is not a sustainable solution.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies that they frequently miss their Definition of Done. What should the Scrum Master suggest? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team improve their processes and consistently meet the Definition of Done. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Lower the Definition of Done standards to make it more achievable.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering standards undermines quality and goes against Scrum principles.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to help the team improve their processes and skills to consistently meet the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team improve their processes to meet quality standards consistently.
answer3: Ignore the issue if the work is mostly done.
explanation3: Incorrect: Meeting the Definition of Done is essential for ensuring quality and usability of the Increment.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to accept incomplete work temporarily.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should not accept incomplete work; all work must meet the Definition of Done.

title: How should the Developers handle non-functional requirements? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Non-functional requirements are treated as Product Backlog items and must be addressed during the Sprint like any other work. This approach ensures that quality is maintained throughout the development process. The Scrum Team ensures quality by adhering to the Definition of Done and addressing all requirements, both functional and non-functional. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Include them in the Product Backlog and address them like any other item.
explanation1: Correct: Non-functional requirements should be included and prioritized in the Product Backlog.
answer2: Ignore them as they are not a primary focus in Scrum.
explanation2: Incorrect: Non-functional requirements are crucial for the quality of the product.
answer3: Handle them during a special hardening Sprint before release.
explanation3: Incorrect: Scrum does not endorse special hardening Sprints; quality should be built in every Sprint.
answer4: Assign them to a specialist outside the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: All work, including non-functional requirements, is managed by the Developers within the team.

title: What is the best way for a Scrum Team to handle technical spikes that are required to explore new technologies? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Including technical spikes in the Product Backlog and planning them in Sprints ensures they are managed transparently and contribute to informed decision-making. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Include the technical spike as a Product Backlog item and plan it as part of the Sprint.
explanation1: Correct: Planning technical spikes as part of the Sprint allows the team to allocate time for exploration without compromising other work.
answer2: Avoid doing technical spikes to prevent disruption to planned tasks.
explanation2: Incorrect: Technical spikes are necessary to gain insights and make informed decisions about new technologies.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to handle technical spikes separately from the Scrum Team’s work.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Developers are responsible for managing technical aspects and need to conduct spikes themselves.
answer4: Conduct spikes informally without tracking them in the Sprint Backlog.
explanation4: Incorrect: Untracked work can disrupt Sprint focus and makes it hard to measure impact and progress.

title: Which actions can a Scrum Master take to help the Developers manage high technical debt? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master can facilitate discussions during backlog refinement to help the team prioritize technical debt, ensuring it is managed alongside new feature development. Scrum Teams ensure quality by addressing technical debt as part of their work. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the team to ignore technical debt and focus on new features.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring technical debt can lead to bigger problems and lower product quality.
answer2: Facilitate discussions on addressing technical debt during Product Backlog Refinement.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating discussions helps the team prioritize technical debt alongside new work.
answer3: Assign specific Developers to handle all technical debt items.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should collectively manage technical debt, not delegate it to specific individuals.
answer4: Remove all technical debt items from the Product Backlog to simplify planning.
explanation4: Incorrect: Technical debt needs to be visible in the backlog to be managed effectively.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing product value by managing the Product Backlog effectively. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner’s primary accountability is to maximize the product’s value through effective backlog management.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is directly accountable for the value delivered by the Scrum Team.

title: True or False: The Scrum Master is responsible for ensuring the team meets their Definition of Done. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the team in meeting their Definition of Done but does not enforce it; the responsibility lies with the Developers. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not enforce the Definition of Done; the team is collectively responsible.
explanation2: Correct: The Developers are responsible for meeting the Definition of Done, with the Scrum Master supporting them by fostering good practices.

title: Which three responsibilities are part of the Product Owner's role? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog, ensures its transparency, and communicates the Product Goal to the team. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ordering the Product Backlog to maximize product value.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner prioritizes the Product Backlog to maximize value.
answer2: Creating the Definition of Done for the team.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is collaboratively defined by the team, not solely by the Product Owner.
answer3: Ensuring the Product Backlog is transparent, visible, and understood.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for maintaining the Product Backlog’s clarity and accessibility.
answer4: Facilitating all Scrum events.
explanation4: Incorrect: Facilitation of events is primarily the responsibility of the Scrum Master.
answer5: Communicating the Product Goal and vision to the team.
explanation5: Correct: The Product Owner ensures the team understands the Product Goal and vision.

title: A Scrum Team is consistently missing their Sprint Goals. What actions should the Scrum Master take to help them? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the Retrospective to address challenges and coach the team on effective Sprint Planning to improve their performance. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team understand and adhere to Scrum theory, practices, and rules. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Facilitate a Sprint Retrospective to identify root causes.
explanation1: Correct: The Retrospective is an opportunity to reflect on performance and plan improvements.
answer2: Increase the team’s working hours to meet the goals.
explanation2: Incorrect: Overworking is not a sustainable solution and contradicts Scrum values.
answer3: Coach the team on realistic Sprint Planning.
explanation3: Correct: Coaching can help the team better forecast and plan their work.
answer4: Report the team’s failures to management for oversight.
explanation4: Incorrect: Issues should be addressed within the team rather than escalating to management.
answer5: Assign tasks based on individual strengths.
explanation5: Incorrect: In Scrum, Developers self-organize and choose their work.

title: Which two actions are crucial for the Scrum Master to ensure the effectiveness of the Scrum Team? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master’s role includes facilitating events and helping the team address impediments to maintain their effectiveness. The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team by helping them improve their practices and effectiveness. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Facilitating Scrum events to ensure they are productive.
explanation1: Correct: The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events occur and are effective.
answer2: Assigning tasks to Developers based on their strengths.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Scrum Team is self-managing, and the Scrum Master does not assign tasks.
answer3: Helping the team identify and remove impediments.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Master actively supports the team in overcoming obstacles to progress.
answer4: Managing the Product Backlog prioritization.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for the Product Backlog, not the Scrum Master.
answer5: Creating the Sprint Goal for the team.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal is defined collaboratively by the Developers and Product Owner.

title: Which two actions should the Scrum Master take if the team is struggling to complete work by the end of the Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate team discussions during the Retrospective and provide coaching to help the team focus and manage impediments effectively. The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team in several ways, including removing impediments to the team’s progress. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Extend the Sprint duration to allow more time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.
answer2: Facilitate a conversation during the Sprint Retrospective to identify improvements.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective allows the team to inspect and adapt to improve performance.
answer3: Reduce the scope of the Sprint Backlog immediately.
explanation3: Incorrect: Adjustments should be made collaboratively with the Product Owner, not unilaterally.
answer4: Coach the team on maintaining focus and removing impediments.
explanation4: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team focus on delivering the Sprint Goal by removing obstacles.
answer5: Report the issue to stakeholders and seek external support.
explanation5: Incorrect: Issues within the team should be resolved internally through coaching and facilitation.

title: Which two responsibilities does the Product Owner have in managing the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for ensuring the Product Backlog is well managed, ordered, and transparent, maximizing value for the team and stakeholders. The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, including its content, availability, and ordering. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensuring the Product Backlog is visible, transparent, and clear to all stakeholders.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner ensures the Product Backlog is accessible and clear to all relevant parties.
answer2: Setting the daily tasks for the Developers.
explanation2: Incorrect: Developers self-manage and select their tasks independently.
answer3: Ordering the Product Backlog items to maximize value.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog to ensure the team works on the most valuable items first.
answer4: Assigning work to Developers during the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Developers decide how to organize and complete their work during the Sprint.
answer5: Approving the Definition of Done for the team.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a shared agreement within the Scrum Team, not solely determined by the Product Owner.

title: A Developer consistently volunteers to take on additional tasks, often leading to incomplete work by the end of the Sprint. How should the Scrum Master address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team manage workload effectively, promoting realistic commitments and preventing burnout. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the Developer to continue volunteering to ensure maximum productivity.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overcommitting can lead to burnout and disrupts the team’s ability to meet the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on the importance of realistic commitments and balancing workload across the team.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team find balance and ensures commitments are achievable.
answer3: Reassign some of the Developer’s tasks to others without discussion.
explanation3: Incorrect: Task reassignment should be discussed openly with the team to maintain transparency and collaboration.
answer4: Ignore the issue as long as the Developer manages to complete most tasks.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring overcommitment can lead to decreased quality and morale over time.

title: A Developer is frequently late to the Daily Scrum, disrupting the flow of the meeting. How should the Scrum Master handle this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should address attendance issues by facilitating a conversation with the Developer to encourage regular participation. The Daily Scrum improves communication, identifies impediments, and promotes quick decision-making. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developer to provide a written update instead of attending the Daily Scrum.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is meant for real-time collaboration, not for reporting.
answer2: Facilitate a conversation with the Developer to understand the reasons and encourage timely participation.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master addresses attendance issues constructively to maintain team collaboration.
answer3: Ignore the lateness and continue the meeting without them.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring the issue can lead to ongoing disruptions and affect team dynamics.
answer4: Exclude the Developer from the Daily Scrum until they can commit to attending on time.
explanation4: Incorrect: Exclusion is not a constructive approach and could harm team morale.

title: A Product Owner feels overwhelmed with managing the Product Backlog. How can the Scrum Master assist? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master can coach the Product Owner on effective techniques for managing the Product Backlog, helping them better organize and prioritize work. The Scrum Master helps the Product Owner in finding effective Product Backlog management techniques. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Take over the Product Owner’s responsibilities temporarily.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should support but not take over responsibilities of the Product Owner.
answer2: Coach the Product Owner on effective backlog management techniques.
explanation2: Correct: Coaching helps the Product Owner refine their approach to managing the Product Backlog efficiently.
answer3: Ask the Developers to help manage the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for the backlog, though Developers can provide input.
answer4: Ignore the situation as it is the Product Owner’s role to manage.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should support and guide, not ignore the challenges faced by the Product Owner.

title: A Scrum Team faces a technical impediment that none of the team members can resolve on their own. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master facilitates the resolution of impediments by helping the team find the necessary resources, including external expertise when needed. The Scrum Master is accountable for removing impediments to the Scrum Team’s progress. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Solve the problem directly as the Scrum Master.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not solve technical issues directly.
answer2: Encourage the team to find external help or expertise.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should facilitate finding the necessary expertise to resolve the impediment.
answer3: Report the issue to management and wait for a solution.
explanation3: Incorrect: Waiting for external solutions does not align with the Scrum Master’s proactive facilitation role.
answer4: Ignore the issue if it doesn’t seem critical.
explanation4: Incorrect: All impediments should be addressed to ensure team progress.

title: A Scrum Team is facing frequent interruptions during their Sprints from external stakeholders. How should the Scrum Master address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to establish clear communication boundaries, ensuring the team remains focused while maintaining stakeholder engagement as needed. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Instruct the team to ignore all external communications during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring stakeholders entirely can lead to missed information and misalignment.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to establish clear boundaries and protocols for managing external communication during Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: Setting clear boundaries helps protect the team's focus while ensuring necessary communication is managed appropriately.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to handle all communication with external stakeholders directly.
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Product Owner manages stakeholder expectations, communication protocols should be established collectively.
answer4: Allow stakeholders to provide feedback only during the Sprint Review to minimize disruptions.
explanation4: Incorrect: Feedback should be managed appropriately, but completely limiting it to the Sprint Review may not be practical or responsive.

title: During a Sprint, a Developer encounters a complex technical issue that could delay the completion of the Sprint Goal. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate a collaborative discussion among Developers to address technical challenges, helping the team stay focused on achieving the Sprint Goal. The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team by helping them improve their practices. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developer to work extra hours to resolve the issue.
explanation1: Incorrect: Encouraging overwork is not a sustainable or effective solution.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion among the Developers to explore possible solutions.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should help the team identify and address challenges through collaboration.
answer3: Escalate the problem to management for a quick fix.
explanation3: Incorrect: Issues should be handled within the Scrum Team, not escalated to management.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to give the team more time to solve the issue.
explanation4: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint goes against Scrum principles.

title: During a Sprint, a key team member becomes unavailable unexpectedly. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team assess the impact of absences and adapt their plan as necessary to maintain progress toward the Sprint Goal. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team remove impediments to the team’s progress. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Reassign the absent member’s tasks to other Developers to ensure continuity.
explanation1: Incorrect: Task reassignment should be handled collectively to maintain team collaboration and balance.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the team to assess the impact and adjust the Sprint plan if necessary.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team adapt to changes by collaboratively assessing and adjusting the plan.
answer3: Extend the Sprint to accommodate the absence and allow for task completion.
explanation3: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint is not allowed and disrupts the regular Scrum cadence.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to reprioritize the Sprint Backlog based on the new team capacity.
explanation4: Incorrect: While adjustments may be needed, the team should collectively decide how to handle the situation first.

title: During a Sprint, the Scrum Master notices that the Developers are frequently interrupted by stakeholders. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach stakeholders to communicate primarily through the Product Owner, helping to protect the Developers' focus. The Scrum Master helps everyone understand Scrum theory and practice. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Inform stakeholders that they need to wait for the Sprint Review to provide feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Feedback and communication should happen continuously, but interruptions should be managed.
answer2: Coach stakeholders to use the Product Owner as their main point of contact.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner manages stakeholder communication, ensuring Developers stay focused.
answer3: Ask the Developers to handle stakeholder interruptions themselves.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should help protect the Developers from unnecessary interruptions.
answer4: Invite stakeholders to attend the Daily Scrum to get updates.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers, not for stakeholder updates.

title: True or False: The Product Backlog refinement process involves the Product Owner and Developers working together to ensure items are ready for future Sprints. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Product Backlog refinement involves the Product Owner and Developers collaborating to ensure items are clear and ready for future Sprints. The Product Owner and Developers collaborate on Product Backlog refinement as needed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: Product Backlog refinement is a collaborative effort between the Product Owner and Developers to clarify and prepare items.
explanation2: Incorrect: Refinement is a shared responsibility between the Product Owner and Developers.

title: Which three activities help ensure that the Product Backlog remains clear and actionable? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Regular refinement, stakeholder involvement, and using feedback from Sprint Reviews help ensure the Product Backlog remains clear, actionable, and aligned with evolving needs. Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity to keep the backlog in good condition. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Only updating the Product Backlog when major issues arise.
explanation1: Incorrect: Regular refinement keeps the backlog manageable and aligned with current priorities.
answer2: Conducting regular refinement sessions to add detail, estimates, and adjust the order of items.
explanation2: Correct: Regular refinement ensures that the backlog reflects the latest understanding of the product needs.
answer3: Involving stakeholders in refinement sessions to provide feedback and insights.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder involvement ensures that the backlog reflects real-world needs and market conditions.
answer4: Waiting until Sprint Planning to review and clarify backlog items.
explanation4: Incorrect: Clarifying items only during Sprint Planning can lead to rushed decisions and misaligned work.
answer5: Using feedback from Sprint Reviews to adjust priorities and refine upcoming items.
explanation5: Correct: Feedback from Sprint Reviews helps align the backlog with stakeholder expectations and product goals.

title: Which three components are included in the Sprint Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog includes selected Product Backlog items, the Sprint Goal, and the plan for achieving that goal. The Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work that the Developers plan to accomplish during the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Selected Product Backlog items.
explanation1: Correct: These items represent the work planned for the Sprint.
answer2: A detailed task list for each Developer.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog does not contain task lists; it’s a plan by the Developers.
answer3: The Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Correct: The Sprint Goal provides focus and direction for the Sprint.
answer4: A plan for achieving the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Correct: The plan outlines how the team will deliver the Increment.
answer5: The Definition of Done.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a separate artifact that guides quality, not part of the Sprint Backlog.

title: Which three elements should be considered when defining a Scrum Team’s Definition of Ready? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Establishing clear acceptance criteria, managing dependencies, and assessing size and complexity help define a useful Definition of Ready, supporting effective Sprint Planning. The Definition of Ready ensures that Product Backlog items are well-prepared for upcoming Sprints. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensuring all items have complete technical specifications before refinement.
explanation1: Incorrect: Refinement should focus on clarity and actionability, not overly detailed specifications.
answer2: Establishing clear acceptance criteria that guide what is needed for an item to be considered ready.
explanation2: Correct: Acceptance criteria help ensure items are actionable and well-understood by the team.
answer3: Identifying and managing dependencies that could affect the item’s implementation.
explanation3: Correct: Managing dependencies early helps prevent delays and ensure smooth progress during the Sprint.
answer4: Including a review by stakeholders before items are refined.
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback but do not directly participate in the refinement process.
answer5: Assessing the size and complexity of items to ensure they are suitable for a single Sprint.
explanation5: Correct: Understanding the size and complexity helps the team commit to work that is feasible within the Sprint.

title: Which two key responsibilities does the Product Owner have during backlog refinement? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner prioritizes items and collaborates with Developers during refinement to ensure that the Product Backlog is clear and aligned with current needs. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Prioritizing Product Backlog items based on stakeholder input and market conditions.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner is responsible for ensuring the backlog reflects current priorities and stakeholder needs.
answer2: Establishing the estimates for each Product Backlog item to guide planning.
explanation2: Incorrect: Estimation is the responsibility of the Developers, not the Product Owner.
answer3: Collaborating with the Developers to clarify items and ensure they are ready for future Sprints.
explanation3: Correct: Collaboration ensures that backlog items are clear, actionable, and properly understood by the team.
answer4: Handling all refinement independently to maintain control over the product direction.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement should be a collaborative effort between the Product Owner and the team.
answer5: Delegating refinement tasks to stakeholders for better market alignment.
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide input, but refinement is managed by the Scrum Team.

title: Which two roles collaborate most closely during Product Backlog refinement to ensure items are ready for future Sprints? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner and Developers collaborate closely during refinement to ensure Product Backlog items are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints. Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity to keep the backlog in good condition. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Scrum Master and Developers
explanation1: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master facilitates refinement, the Product Owner leads the effort with the Developers.
answer2: Product Owner and Developers
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner and Developers collaborate to refine items, ensuring clarity and readiness for future Sprints.
answer3: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner leads refinement, while the Scrum Master supports by facilitating the process.
answer4: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback, but the Product Owner and Developers manage refinement.
answer5: Product Owner and Scrum Master
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement is a collaborative process led by the Product Owner with support from the Developers.

title: A Scrum Team frequently struggles to start work on Sprint Backlog items due to missing information. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate refinement sessions to ensure that Product Backlog items are clear and ready, minimizing delays caused by missing information. Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity to keep the backlog in good condition. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign a Developer to gather the missing information before the work begins.
explanation1: Incorrect: Information gathering should be a collaborative effort, not the responsibility of a single team member.
answer2: Facilitate refinement sessions to ensure Product Backlog items are well-defined and ready before they are pulled into a Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement sessions help ensure that items are clear, actionable, and prepared for the team to start work.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to provide all details upfront before adding items to the Sprint Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner provides input, but the Developers should collaborate to refine items as needed.
answer4: Ignore the issue, assuming the team will learn to handle incomplete information over time.
explanation4: Incorrect: Proactively addressing the refinement process is key to maintaining Sprint efficiency.

title: What is the main function of the Product Backlog in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog is a prioritized list of all work needed for the product, managed by the Product Owner and continuously updated to reflect changes. The Product Backlog is an ordered list of everything that is known to be needed in the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To assign tasks to individual Developers.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is not for task assignment; it’s a prioritized list of work needed for the product.
answer2: To provide a dynamic, prioritized list of all work needed to enhance the product.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog is continuously updated and managed by the Product Owner to maximize value.
answer3: To track the team’s performance throughout the project.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog focuses on future work, not on tracking performance.
answer4: To ensure all team members have an equal amount of work.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog prioritizes work to maximize value, not to distribute workload evenly.

title: What is the most effective way for a Scrum Team to ensure that Product Backlog refinement is productive? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Product Backlog refinement should involve regular, time-boxed sessions with active participation from the Product Owner and Developers to ensure clarity and preparedness. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the Product Owner to lead the session and dictate what needs to be refined.
explanation1: Incorrect: While the Product Owner plays a key role, refinement should be a collaborative process involving the entire team.
answer2: Ensure regular, time-boxed sessions are held, with active participation from both the Product Owner and Developers.
explanation2: Correct: Regular, time-boxed refinement sessions promote ongoing alignment and preparedness for upcoming Sprints.
answer3: Skip refinement sessions if the backlog seems clear enough.
explanation3: Incorrect: Consistent refinement helps maintain a well-understood and prioritized backlog, even when things seem clear.
answer4: Assign a specific Developer to handle refinement and report back to the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement is a shared responsibility and benefits from the collective input of the team.

title: Which approach should a Scrum Team take if they frequently encounter unclear requirements during Sprint Planning? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should facilitate refinement sessions to clarify requirements before Sprint Planning, ensuring that items are well-understood and ready for commitment. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Proceed with the unclear requirements and adjust as more information becomes available.
explanation1: Incorrect: Proceeding without clarity can lead to misaligned work and incomplete Increments.
answer2: Facilitate a refinement session before Sprint Planning to clarify requirements and ensure items are ready.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement sessions help the team clarify requirements, making Sprint Planning more efficient and effective.
answer3: Ignore the unclear requirements and focus on items that are well understood.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring unclear requirements without addressing them can lead to backlog mismanagement.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to refine all items independently before the next Sprint Planning.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement should be a collaborative effort involving both the Product Owner and Developers.

title: True or False: During the Daily Scrum, each Developer must provide an update on their progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum focuses on how each Developer’s progress contributes to achieving the Sprint Goal and planning the next steps. The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and how to plan the next 24 hours.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is about inspecting progress and adapting plans to meet the Sprint Goal.

title: True or False: The Sprint Review focuses on evaluating the team's performance rather than inspecting the Increment. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review is an event for inspecting the Increment and adapting the Product Backlog based on feedback, not for evaluating the team’s performance. The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is focused on the Increment and gathering feedback, not on evaluating the team’s performance.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review is a collaborative event where the Increment is inspected, and feedback is gathered to adapt the Product Backlog.

title: Which three best practices can help improve the effectiveness of the Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Retrospectives involve structured facilitation, equal participation, and setting actionable outcomes to drive team improvement. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensure all team members are given equal time to speak.
explanation1: Correct: Equal participation helps gather diverse insights and fosters a collaborative environment.
answer2: Focus only on the negative aspects of the last Sprint.
explanation2: Incorrect: Retrospectives should balance positives, negatives, and opportunities for improvement.
answer3: Use facilitation techniques to guide the conversation constructively.
explanation3: Correct: Effective facilitation helps keep discussions focused and productive.
answer4: Schedule the Retrospective as a casual, unstructured conversation.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Retrospective should be structured to ensure meaningful outcomes.
answer5: Set specific, actionable items for improvement.
explanation5: Correct: Actionable outcomes drive continuous improvement and accountability.

title: During the Sprint Review, the team finds that stakeholders are not engaging with the presented Increment. What action should the Scrum Master take? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should address engagement issues by improving communication and understanding stakeholder expectations, making the Sprint Review more effective. The Scrum Master ensures that stakeholders understand and support the review process. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Discuss the issue with stakeholders to understand their expectations.
explanation1: Correct: Understanding stakeholder needs can improve engagement.
answer2: Make the Sprint Review more formal to encourage participation.
explanation2: Incorrect: Formality does not necessarily increase engagement.
answer3: Facilitate better communication between the team and stakeholders.
explanation3: Correct: Effective facilitation can bridge gaps and encourage active participation.
answer4: Change the Increment presentation format based on stakeholder feedback.
explanation4: Incorrect: Presentation changes should be based on team discussions, not just external feedback.
answer5: Ignore the issue as it does not impact the team's work directly.
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback is crucial to the Scrum process.

title: Which two factors should the Developers consider when selecting items for the Sprint Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Developers should consider their capacity and the complexity of items when selecting work for the Sprint Backlog, ensuring they commit to achievable and valuable tasks. Developers create a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog, and adapt their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: The Product Owner’s personal preferences.
explanation1: Incorrect: Selection should be based on the Product Goal and the team’s capacity, not personal preferences.
answer2: The capacity of the team to complete the work within the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Understanding their capacity helps the team select a realistic amount of work for the Sprint.
answer3: The complexity and size of the items.
explanation3: Correct: Considering complexity and size helps the team plan realistically for what can be completed in the Sprint.
answer4: The length of the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: While Sprint length is fixed, the team’s capacity and item complexity are more directly relevant.
answer5: Stakeholder expectations.
explanation5: Incorrect: While important, direct stakeholder expectations are managed by the Product Owner, not by the Developers during planning.

title: A Scrum Team has noticed that their Daily Scrums are becoming long and unfocused. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master ensures that the Daily Scrum remains focused and time-boxed, facilitating it if necessary to keep the team aligned. The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and is kept within the 15-minute time-box. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Cancel the Daily Scrum until the team is better organized.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is essential and cannot be canceled.
answer2: Facilitate the Daily Scrum to keep it focused and within the timebox.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master ensures the event remains productive and adheres to the 15-minute timebox.
answer3: Increase the duration of the Daily Scrum to cover all topics.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is strictly time-boxed to 15 minutes.
answer4: Allow the Developers to conduct it informally without structure.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum should have a clear structure to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers are unsure about how much work they can take on. What is the best course of action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should start with a manageable amount of work and use their experience to adjust in future Sprints, ensuring realistic and achievable commitments. Developers create a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog, and adapt their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Commit to as much work as possible to push their limits.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overcommitting can lead to burnout and unmet Sprint Goals.
answer2: Start with a manageable amount of work and adjust future Sprints based on their capacity.
explanation2: Correct: The team should commit to what they are confident they can achieve and adjust based on experience.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to decide how much work they should take on.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Developers are responsible for planning their work; the Scrum Master facilitates but does not decide.
answer4: Skip Sprint Planning and start working immediately to save time.
explanation4: Incorrect: Planning is crucial for setting clear expectations and aligning on the Sprint Goal.

title: During the Daily Scrum, one Developer dominates the conversation, leaving little room for others to speak. How should the Scrum Master address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should remind the team of the purpose of the Daily Scrum and encourage equal participation, ensuring effective communication among all members. The Daily Scrum improves communication, identifies impediments, and promotes quick decision-making. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Let the Developer continue as long as they are providing valuable input.
explanation1: Incorrect: Dominating the conversation prevents balanced participation and collaboration.
answer2: Gently remind the team of the purpose of the Daily Scrum and encourage equal participation.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master ensures that all team members have the opportunity to contribute, promoting balanced communication.
answer3: Interrupt the Developer and move on to the next team member immediately.
explanation3: Incorrect: Abrupt interruptions can create tension and reduce the effectiveness of the meeting.
answer4: Assign specific time slots for each team member to speak.
explanation4: Incorrect: Time slots can make the meeting feel rigid and hinder natural discussion flow.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies communication as a recurring problem. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team address and improve their communication practices. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign a team member to act as the communication manager.
explanation1: Incorrect: Roles should not be added; the team should work on improving communication collectively.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on how the team can improve communication practices during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team identify and implement improvements.
answer3: Ignore the issue as it's the team's responsibility.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master plays a key role in helping the team improve.
answer4: Document communication rules and enforce them strictly.
explanation4: Incorrect: Strict rules can hinder flexibility; the focus should be on continuous improvement.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders frequently question the prioritization of completed work. How should the Scrum Master address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate open discussions during the Sprint Review to capture stakeholder feedback, helping the team align future work with stakeholder priorities. The Sprint Review is a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Product Owner to justify every prioritization decision made during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Justification may create tension and detracts from the collaborative nature of the Sprint Review.
answer2: Facilitate open discussions during the Sprint Review to capture stakeholder feedback and ensure it informs future prioritization decisions.
explanation2: Correct: Engaging stakeholders in open discussions helps ensure their feedback is considered in the backlog prioritization process.
answer3: Ignore the feedback to keep the meeting focused solely on the Increment demonstration.
explanation3: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback is valuable and should inform future decisions.
answer4: End the Sprint Review early if stakeholders disagree with prioritization to prevent conflict.
explanation4: Incorrect: Avoiding conflict does not address underlying concerns and hinders constructive feedback.

title: During the Sprint, a Developer encounters a technical challenge that is delaying their progress. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum allows the Developers to inspect progress and discuss any challenges, ensuring that impediments are addressed promptly to keep the Sprint on track. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Work extra hours to make up for the delay.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overworking is not sustainable and does not address the root cause of the challenge.
answer2: Bring up the challenge during the Daily Scrum and collaborate with the team to find a solution.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum is the ideal time to discuss impediments and seek team collaboration to resolve challenges.
answer3: Ignore the challenge and focus on other tasks.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring challenges can lead to missed goals and compromised quality.
answer4: Wait until the Sprint Retrospective to discuss the challenge.
explanation4: Incorrect: Challenges should be addressed immediately, not delayed until the Retrospective.

title: Who should attend the Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Retrospective is a key event for the entire Scrum Team to reflect on their work and identify ways to improve their processes. The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint. It is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect itself and create a plan for improvements. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Only the Scrum Master and the Product Owner
explanation1: Incorrect: The entire Scrum Team should participate in the Retrospective.
answer2: Only the Developers
explanation2: Incorrect: The Retrospective involves all members of the Scrum Team, not just Developers.
answer3: The entire Scrum Team
explanation3: Correct: The Sprint Retrospective is for the entire Scrum Team to inspect and adapt their processes.
answer4: The Product Owner and stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders do not participate in the Retrospective.

title: Which event allows the Scrum Team to present the Increment and gather feedback from stakeholders? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review allows the Scrum Team to present the Increment to stakeholders and gather feedback to adapt the Product Backlog. The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Sprint Planning
explanation1: Incorrect: Sprint Planning focuses on defining the work for the Sprint, not presenting the Increment.
answer2: Sprint Review
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review is the event where the team presents the Increment and gathers feedback.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum focuses on team progress and planning, not stakeholder feedback.
answer4: Sprint Retrospective
explanation4: Incorrect: The Retrospective is for team reflection, not for stakeholder engagement.

title: What is the primary purpose of the Sprint Review? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review is held to inspect the Increment, gather feedback, and adapt the Product Backlog as needed. The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To finalize the product for release.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is not for finalizing products but for inspecting the Increment and gathering feedback.
answer2: To inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog based on feedback.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review focuses on reviewing completed work and adapting the backlog based on stakeholder feedback.
answer3: To review the team's performance.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is focused on the product, not the team’s performance.
answer4: To present completed tasks to the Product Owner.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Review involves stakeholders and focuses on the overall Increment, not just individual tasks.

title: What is the main purpose of the Sprint Planning in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Sprint Planning sets the direction of the Sprint by defining what can be delivered and how the team will work to achieve the Sprint Goal. The purpose of Sprint Planning is to define what can be delivered in the Sprint and how that work will be achieved. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To assign tasks to each team member based on their strengths.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers self-organize and decide how to complete the work themselves.
answer2: To set the direction of the Sprint by defining what can be delivered and how to achieve it.
explanation2: Correct: Sprint Planning defines the scope and plan for the Sprint.
answer3: To evaluate the team’s performance from the previous Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Performance evaluation is not the focus of Sprint Planning; it sets the agenda for the upcoming Sprint.
answer4: To present the Sprint Backlog to stakeholders for approval.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog is created for the team’s use, not for stakeholder approval.

title: The team has completed all work in the Sprint Backlog before the end of the Sprint. What should they do next? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: If the team finishes their planned work early, they should collaborate with the Product Owner to identify additional work that can be pulled into the Sprint, maintaining productivity. The Sprint Backlog is updated throughout the Sprint as more is learned. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Relax until the next Sprint starts.
explanation1: Incorrect: Time in the Sprint should be used productively to improve the Increment or address other work.
answer2: Collaborate with the Product Owner to pull additional work from the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The team can collaborate with the Product Owner to select more work if capacity allows.
answer3: End the Sprint early and start a new one.
explanation3: Incorrect: Sprints should not be ended early, even if work is completed.
answer4: Conduct the Sprint Review immediately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Review occurs at the end of the Sprint, not earlier.

title: The Product Owner wants to include more items in the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should discuss any proposed changes to the Sprint Backlog collaboratively, ensuring that they understand the impact on the Sprint Goal and make informed decisions. The Developers can adjust their plan each day during the Sprint, and adjust the Sprint Backlog as needed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the changes to maintain good relations with the Product Owner.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes during the Sprint should be minimized to maintain focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Discuss the impact of the changes with the Scrum Team and decide collaboratively.
explanation2: Correct: Any changes to the Sprint Backlog should be discussed and agreed upon by the entire team, considering the impact on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Reject the changes outright to avoid any disruptions.
explanation3: Incorrect: Feedback should be considered, but it should be managed thoughtfully.
answer4: Extend the Sprint duration to accommodate the additional work.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended to include more work.

title: How can the Scrum Master best support the Scrum Team in improving their velocity? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master can best support the team by facilitating Retrospectives focused on continuous improvement, helping the team identify and address impediments that affect their velocity. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices, within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Push the team to take on more work each Sprint to increase output.
explanation1: Incorrect: Pushing more work onto the team can lead to burnout and decreased quality.
answer2: Facilitate Retrospectives focused on identifying process improvements and removing impediments.
explanation2: Correct: Retrospectives are key to identifying areas for improvement and enhancing the team’s efficiency and effectiveness.
answer3: Assign more Developers to the team to increase capacity.
explanation3: Incorrect: Simply adding more people does not guarantee improved velocity and can disrupt the team dynamics.
answer4: Extend Sprints to allow more time for completing tasks.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed to encourage efficiency and should not be extended.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Product Owner wants to add a high-priority item, but the Developers feel it would compromise the Sprint Goal. How should this be handled? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The team should collaborate with the Product Owner to discuss the implications and decide how best to proceed, maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal. The Developers plan the work necessary to create an Increment that meets the Definition of Done. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Add the item and try to adjust other tasks to fit it in.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding new items that compromise the Sprint Goal is not recommended.
answer2: Discuss the implications with the Product Owner and adjust priorities if necessary.
explanation2: Correct: Open communication about priorities and capacity is key to maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Reject the new item outright to stick to the plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Team should collaborate on how best to proceed with new information.
answer4: End the Sprint and plan a new one to include the high-priority item.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints should not be ended early unless the goal is no longer relevant.

title: A Scrum Team is frequently missing their Sprint Goals due to unclear requirements. How should this be addressed? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Product Backlog Refinement sessions allow the Scrum Team to collaboratively clarify requirements, ensuring that items are well understood and ready for Sprint Planning. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Blame the Product Owner for not providing clear requirements.
explanation1: Incorrect: Blame is not productive; the team should work together to improve clarity.
answer2: Collaborate during Product Backlog Refinement to clarify requirements before Sprint Planning.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement sessions help ensure that requirements are clear and actionable, improving Sprint outcomes.
answer3: Skip the unclear items and focus only on well-defined work.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should refine unclear items to ensure they are ready for future Sprints.
answer4: Request more time for each Sprint to understand the requirements better.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed, and understanding requirements should be part of refinement, not extended Sprints.

title: What is the purpose of the Definition of Done? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done ensures transparency by providing a clear standard for what constitutes completion of work, ensuring quality and shared understanding among team members. The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To provide a checklist of tasks for the Developers.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a quality standard, not just a task list.
answer2: To ensure transparency and understanding of what has been completed.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done provides clarity on when work meets the necessary standards.
answer3: To dictate the acceptance criteria for all Product Backlog items.
explanation3: Incorrect: Acceptance criteria are specific to Product Backlog items and not solely the Definition of Done.
answer4: To allow the Product Owner to control quality standards.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a shared understanding within the Scrum Team, not controlled by one role.

title: Which of the following actions can improve the transparency of the Product Backlog? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Regular refinement of the Product Backlog with the Scrum Team and stakeholders improves transparency, ensuring everyone understands and is aligned with the priorities. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Keep the backlog updates internal to the Scrum Team to avoid confusion.
explanation1: Incorrect: Transparency requires that updates are visible to all stakeholders, not hidden.
answer2: Regularly refine the backlog with the entire Scrum Team and stakeholders.
explanation2: Correct: Refining the backlog regularly with the team and stakeholders ensures it remains transparent and well-understood.
answer3: Only update the backlog at the start of each Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: The backlog should be continuously refined, not just updated at Sprint start.
answer4: Limit access to the backlog to avoid unnecessary changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: Restricting access reduces transparency and stakeholder involvement.

title: Which three actions best help maintain the transparency of the Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Transparency of the Product Backlog is maintained through regular updates, collaborative refinement, and stakeholder engagement, ensuring it accurately represents the work ahead. The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, including its content, availability, and ordering. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Regularly updating the backlog with new information.
explanation1: Correct: Regular updates ensure the backlog reflects the latest priorities and insights.
answer2: Allowing only the Product Owner to make changes.
explanation2: Incorrect: While the Product Owner is accountable, the whole Scrum Team collaborates on refinement.
answer3: Refining backlog items with the team.
explanation3: Correct: Regular refinement sessions help clarify and prepare items for future Sprints.
answer4: Hiding incomplete items from stakeholders.
explanation4: Incorrect: Transparency requires that all items be visible, even those in progress.
answer5: Sharing the Product Backlog with stakeholders for feedback.
explanation5: Correct: Stakeholder feedback ensures that the backlog reflects business needs and priorities.

title: Which three techniques can a Scrum Team use to better manage scope creep during Sprints? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Using the Sprint Goal, regularly reviewing progress, and maintaining open communication help Scrum Teams manage scope creep and maintain focus during Sprints. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team focus on creating high-value Increments. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allowing stakeholders to add items to the Sprint Backlog if they are critical.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes to the Sprint Backlog should be managed through the Product Backlog and agreed upon by the team.
answer2: Using the Sprint Goal as a guide to maintain focus and resist adding non-essential work.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal helps the team stay aligned and resist the urge to take on additional work.
answer3: Regularly reviewing progress during Daily Scrums to ensure the team remains focused on the committed work.
explanation3: Correct: Daily Scrums help the team stay on track and manage any deviations from the Sprint plan.
answer4: Accepting new tasks only if they are quick and easy to complete.
explanation4: Incorrect: Accepting new tasks based on perceived ease can disrupt the Sprint and lead to incomplete work.
answer5: Facilitating open communication about the impact of changes on the Sprint Goal and team capacity.
explanation5: Correct: Open communication helps the team make informed decisions about handling scope changes without compromising the Sprint Goal.

title: Which two approaches can help prevent scope creep during the Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Reinforcing the Sprint Goal and regularly reviewing the Sprint Backlog help maintain focus and prevent scope creep, ensuring that the team delivers on their commitments. Scrum Teams only commit to work selected during Sprint Planning. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Strictly limiting interactions between Developers and stakeholders during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Limiting interactions can cause misalignment and reduce the team’s responsiveness to feedback.
answer2: Reinforcing the importance of the Sprint Goal and managing changes through the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal helps prevent unauthorized scope changes.
answer3: Reviewing the Sprint Backlog regularly to ensure alignment with the Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Correct: Regular review keeps the team focused and prevents deviation from the planned work.
answer4: Allowing urgent changes to be added directly to the Sprint Backlog without discussion.
explanation4: Incorrect: Uncontrolled changes disrupt planning and risk Sprint Goal achievement.
answer5: Only allowing changes if they are approved by the Scrum Master.
explanation5: Incorrect: Changes should be managed collectively through proper Scrum processes, not by individual authority.

title: A Product Owner frequently requests changes during the Sprint, disrupting the team’s focus. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach the Product Owner on managing changes effectively to maintain a stable Sprint Backlog and protect the team’s focus. No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the changes if they are necessary to meet stakeholder demands.
explanation1: Incorrect: Allowing changes mid-Sprint disrupts focus and jeopardizes the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Coach the Product Owner on the importance of maintaining a stable Sprint Backlog during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps protect the team’s focus by managing changes appropriately.
answer3: Ask the Developers to accommodate the changes as best they can.
explanation3: Incorrect: Accommodating changes without proper evaluation can disrupt the Sprint Goal.
answer4: Pause the Sprint until the changes are fully evaluated.
explanation4: Incorrect: Pausing the Sprint is not a solution; changes should be managed through the backlog refinement process.

title: A Scrum Team is frequently unable to complete all tasks planned for the Sprint due to poor estimation. What should the Scrum Master do to help? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate training on estimation techniques, helping the team improve their ability to commit to realistic workloads during Sprints. Estimation helps the Scrum Team forecast progress and manage expectations. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Reduce the number of tasks the team plans for in each Sprint without changing estimation practices.
explanation1: Incorrect: Reducing tasks without improving estimation does not address the root problem and can lead to further misalignment.
answer2: Facilitate training sessions on estimation techniques and encourage the team to use these during refinement and planning.
explanation2: Correct: Training on estimation techniques helps the team make more accurate commitments and improve Sprint planning.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to prioritize simpler tasks to ensure completion.
explanation3: Incorrect: Task prioritization should be based on value and alignment with the Sprint Goal, not task complexity.
answer4: Ignore the issue, assuming the team will naturally improve estimation skills over time.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should actively support the team in refining their estimation techniques.

title: During a Sprint, a stakeholder requests changes to the scope of work that the Developers are currently working on. How should the Scrum Master respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should coach stakeholders to manage changes appropriately through Sprint Planning or backlog refinement, protecting the team’s focus. Changes are only made during the Sprint if the Sprint Goal remains intact. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the changes if they align with the team’s current progress.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes should not disrupt the team’s focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Coach the stakeholder to communicate changes during Sprint Planning or refinement sessions.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master guides stakeholders to follow appropriate channels for scope changes.
answer3: Add the change immediately to keep the stakeholder satisfied.
explanation3: Incorrect: Adding changes mid-Sprint compromises the Sprint Goal and focus.
answer4: Escalate the issue to management to handle the stakeholder’s request.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing scope changes should be handled within the Scrum Team processes.

title: Which approach best supports a Scrum Team in managing urgent customer feedback received mid-Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should capture urgent feedback in the Product Backlog, allowing it to be prioritized and addressed in future Sprints without disrupting the current Sprint. The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Stop the Sprint immediately and adjust the Sprint Backlog to include the feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Stopping the Sprint disrupts the team’s focus and does not align with Scrum principles.
